university: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

documents.title: Educational Technology - Current Students (Generative AI Tools)
documents.summary: The page lists SBMI educational technology and has a short Generative AI Tools section. It warns against putting IP into outside GPTs and points students to UTHealth-hosted or licensed tools (AIChat on Llama, Qualified Health, Copilot, Grammarly). It sets no academic-use rules.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no ban or limit on AI in coursework. It names licensed and hosted AI tools students can use and warns not to put IP into outside GPTs ("unsuitable for inputting Intellectual Property"), so AI use is permitted with data conditions.

units.why: The section defines the technology: "A generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) is a large language model (LLM)". It is a definition that sets what the AI section covers, so informs, general, P61.
units.anchor: A generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) is a large language model (LLM)
units.frag_start: A generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)

units.why: The warning says "All GPTs owned and operated by organizations other than UTHealth should be considered unsuitable for inputting Intellectual Property". This is a data and IP protection rule for anyone using external GPTs, so P50 (protect data), should-not, with privacy-data and IP topics.
units.anchor: unsuitable for inputting Intellectual Property(IP) or copyrighted information
units.frag_start: Warning: All GPTs owned and operated
units.policy: External GPTs not owned and operated by UTHealth are unsuitable for inputting intellectual property or copyrighted information such as dissertations and research data.
units.fit_note: Also names IP and copyrighted material (dissertations, research data), which P50 only partly covers.

units.why: The sentence "There is no way to extract/recall data input into a GPT owned and operated by entities other than UTHealth" explains why input is risky: a fact about data retention, so P50 and informs.
units.anchor: There is no way to extract/recall data input into a GPT
units.frag_start: There is no way

documents.unit: McGovern Medical School (Center for Humanities and Ethics)
documents.title: Policy on AI Generative Tools
documents.summary: The McGovern Center says UTHealth does not ban AI and leaves decisions to faculty, then sets its own rules. Students may use AI in limited situations (concept clarification, editing), must cite it, and may not use it for reflective writing or references. Faculty use AI detection and misuse falls under conduct codes.
documents.stance_why: The Center allows AI only "in limited situations", advises asking for permission for artwork or writing assignments, and bans AI for reflections and references. That is permitted only for narrow listed uses, so restrict.

units.why: The Background defines GPT tools: "ChatGPT is but one example of a GPT (Generative Pretraining Transformer) language model". It sets what the policy covers, so P61, informs, general.
units.anchor: ChatGPT is but one example of a GPT (Generative Pretraining Transformer) language model
units.frag_start: ChatGPT is but one example

units.why: The passage says "AI tools can be used in responsible ways" and urges exploring "their benefits rather than solely focusing on the drawbacks". That is a statement of benefits and balance, not a rule, so P87, informs.
units.anchor: explore their benefits rather than solely focusing on the drawbacks
units.frag_start: Concerns over plagiarism, ethics, and academic integrity

units.why: "artificial hallucination is possible" with citations to non-existent references warns that output may be wrong, so P31 (AI output is often wrong), informs.
units.anchor: artificial hallucination is possible
units.frag_start: AI tools can be helpful, but users should be aware

units.why: "many respected peer-reviewed journals have or are developing policies to prohibit or limit these tools’ use" points to external venue rules on AI, closest to P62 (research and scholarship, deferring to venue rules). It is context only, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: many respected peer-reviewed journals have or are developing policies to prohibit or limit
units.frag_start: Finally, many respected peer-reviewed journals
units.fit_note: Only reports that journals restrict AI; it does not tell students to follow venue rules.

units.why: "UTHealth Houston and McGovern Medical School do not expressly prohibit the use of AI tools... leaving faculty and departments to determine how it may or may not be used". The decision is handed to faculty and departments. I chose P04 (instructor level) over P85 because faculty are named first and the rule is about classes; departments are the P85 part.
units.anchor: do not expressly prohibit the use of AI tools like ChatGPT and others
units.frag_start: UTHealth Houston and McGovern Medical School do not
units.policy: UTHealth Houston and McGovern Medical School do not expressly prohibit AI tools like ChatGPT, leaving faculty and departments to determine how they may or may not be used in classes and educational programs.
units.fit_note: Also leaves the decision to departments, not only instructors (P85).

units.why: The Center says generative tools "should not replace students’ own critical thinking and reflection". That keeps the student as the primary thinker, so P32, should-not.
units.anchor: should not replace students’ own critical thinking and reflection
units.frag_start: The McGovern Center acknowledges that generative tools

units.why: "Students may consult AI generative tools in limited situations" sets the Center's default: AI use only for narrow listed uses. Nothing fits it as a type (P01 is a ban, P02 permits broadly), so UNCOVERED; the stance is restrict.
units.anchor: Students may consult AI generative tools in limited situations.
units.frag_start: Students may consult AI generative tools
units.uncovered_note: Default rule: students may use AI only in narrow listed situations, with other uses needing permission.

units.why: The example list includes "to clarify definitions of terms or differentiate between terms" and to "synthesize information about ethical principles", using AI to understand concepts, so P12, may.
units.anchor: to clarify definitions of terms or differentiate between terms
units.frag_start: Examples: to clarify definitions of terms
units.frag_end: primarily assigned in your program or course
units.policy: Students may consult AI tools to clarify or differentiate terms, synthesize information about ethical principles, and summarize key points from a supplementary text not primarily assigned in the program or course.

units.why: The example "to serve as an editor to review your writing style for grammar, spelling, and organization" is a permission for editing support, so P91, may.
units.anchor: to serve as an editor to review your writing style for grammar, spelling, and organization
units.frag_start: or to serve as an editor

units.why: "There may also be opportunities to explore AI tools as part of an individual or group assignment... clearly described in course or program materials" says AI is sometimes built into assignments, so P79. It also promises the materials will say so, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: opportunities to explore AI tools as part of an individual or group assignment
units.frag_start: There may also be opportunities
units.fit_note: Also says such uses will be clearly described in course or program materials.

units.anchor: advised to contact the program or course director in advance to obtain permission
units.frag_start: If a student plans to use AI generative tools

units.why: "When AI tools are used, they should be cited" asks students to acknowledge any AI use, so P24, should.

units.frag_start: When AI tools are used, they should be cited

units.why: The citation template "Tool Name. (Year, Month Date of query). “Text of query.” Generated using Tool Name." names the tool, the date and the exact prompt, so P25, should.
units.anchor: Tool Name. (Year, Month Date of query). “Text of query.” Generated using Tool Name.
units.frag_start: Tool Name. (Year, Month Date of query).
units.policy: AI citations follow the format: Tool Name. (Year, Month Date of query). “Text of query.” Generated using Tool Name. Link to tool name.

units.why: "students should not use these tools to generate reflections for writing assignments (e.g., journals, reflective essays)" bans AI-produced text for a named class of submitted work, so P19, should-not. The Ground Rules repeat it and are not coded separately.
units.anchor: students should not use these tools to generate reflections for writing assignments

units.why: "they are responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content they submit, regardless of whether they personally authored it or used an AI tool" makes students accountable for submissions, so P29, must in effect.
units.anchor: responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content they submit
units.frag_start: Students are also reminded that they are responsible
units.frag_end: used an AI tool to generate it.

units.why: "Faculty will use AI detection software to identify instances of AI-generated writing in student work" commits faculty to detection, automatic through Turnitin in Canvas. P40 (use detection tools), not P39, because detector output is used, not distrusted.
units.anchor: Faculty will use AI detection software to identify instances of AI-generated writing
units.frag_start: Faculty will use AI detection software
units.frag_end: as part of a Canvas assignment.

units.why: "they may be subject to McGovern Medical School’s code of conduct and UTHealth Houston’s policies on academic dishonesty or misconduct" classifies uncited AI use as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: may be subject to McGovern Medical School’s code of conduct
units.frag_start: If a student is found to have used AI tools

units.why: "policies on plagiarism still apply to any uncited or improperly cited use of work produced by other persons" ties AI use to existing plagiarism rules, so P45 as an existing-rules statement, though it speaks of other persons.

units.frag_start: Remember, policies on plagiarism still apply
units.fit_note: Speaks of work by other persons; AI is not named in this sentence.

units.why: "Do not use these tools to generate references or citations as they may return incorrect information" bans one specific use. P19 covers text submitted as one's own and P31 is a warning, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Do not use these tools to generate references or citations
units.frag_start: Do not use these tools to generate references
units.uncovered_note: Students may not use AI to generate references or citations because it can return citations to works that do not exist.

units.why: "Deviations from this policy will be explicitly outlined in program requirements and course syllabi" says other rules will be stated in syllabi, so P09 (state AI expectations in syllabi), although it is a promise rather than a duty.

units.why: "Students are free to use these apps to help with rephrasing sentences, rearranging paragraphs, grammar, etc., that are otherwise self-written" exempts grammar and style checkers such as Grammarly from the restrictive rule, so P100, may.

notes: No university-wide document found; McGovern Medical School policy used as school layer. SBMI page is mostly tool information, so several units are P92/P50 tool statements. Turnitin and Proctorio entries are not AI policy and are not coded.
